questions.q: Two independent events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(P(A) = \frac{3}{4}\) and \(P(B) = \frac{9}{10}\). Find \(P(A \mathrm{\ and\ } B)\).
questions.answer: Final Answer: \(\frac{27}{40}\). Independent events multiply: \(P(A)\times P(B) = \frac{3}{4}\times\frac{9}{10} = \frac{27}{40}\).

questions.q: A data set of 5 values has a mean of 14. A new value of 44 is added. What is the new mean?
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. Old total \( = 5\times14 = 70 \). New total \( = 70+44 = 114 \). New mean \( = 114/6 = 19 \).
questions.explanation: Old total \( = 5\times14 = 70 \). New total \( = 70+44 = 114 \). New mean \( = 114/6 = 19 \).

A committee of 3 students is to be chosen from a group of 8 candidates. How many different committees can be formed?
questions.answer: Because the order of committee members does not matter, this is a combination: \({}_8C_3 = \binom{8}{3} = \frac{8!}{3!(8 - 3)!} = \frac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = \mathbf{56} \mathrm{\ different\ committees}\)
questions.explanation: Because the order of committee members does not matter, this is a combination: \({}_8C_3 = \binom{8}{3} = \frac{8!}{3!(8 - 3)!} = \frac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = \mathbf{56} \mathrm{\ different\ committees}\)

questions.q: A bivariate regression model for student preparation hours \(x\) and exam grade \(y\) yields the line of best fit \(\hat{y} = 4.8x + 52\). A student who studied for 8 hours scored 94 on the exam. (a) What is the model's predicted score for this student? (b) Compute and interpret the student's regression residual.
questions.answer: (a) Predicted Score \(\hat{y}\): Substitute \(x = 8\) into the regression equation: \(\hat{y} = 4.8(8) + 52 = 38.4 + 52 = \mathbf{90.4}.\) (b) Residual Calculation & Interpretation: \(\mathrm{Residual} = y - \hat{y} = 94 - 90.4 = \mathbf{+3.6}.\) Because the residual is positive (+3.6), the student's actual score was 3.6 points higher than the score predicted by the regression line (the model underestimated the student's performance).
questions.explanation: (a) Predicted Score \(\hat{y}\): Substitute \(x = 8\) into the regression equation: \(\hat{y} = 4.8(8) + 52 = 38.4 + 52 = \mathbf{90.4}.\) (b) Residual Calculation & Interpretation: \(\mathrm{Residual} = y - \hat{y} = 94 - 90.4 = \mathbf{+3.6}.\) Because the residual is positive (+3.6), the student's actual score was 3.6 points higher than the score predicted by the regression line (the model underestimated the student's performance).

questions.q: A random variable \(X\) has outcomes -8, 10, 15, 25 with \( P(X=-8)=\tfrac{1}{20}, P(X=10)=\tfrac{2}{20}, P(X=15)=\tfrac{4}{20}, P(X=25)=\tfrac{13}{20} \). Find \(E(X)\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. \( E(X) = -8\left(\tfrac{1}{20}\right) + 10\left(\tfrac{2}{20}\right) + 15\left(\tfrac{4}{20}\right) + 25\left(\tfrac{13}{20}\right) = \dfrac{397}{20} \).

questions.q: A random variable \(X\) has outcomes -2, 6, 9, 18 with \( P(X=-2)=\tfrac{2}{20}, P(X=6)=\tfrac{1}{20}, P(X=9)=\tfrac{14}{20}, P(X=18)=\tfrac{3}{20} \). Find \(E(X)\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. \( E(X) = -2\left(\tfrac{2}{20}\right) + 6\left(\tfrac{1}{20}\right) + 9\left(\tfrac{14}{20}\right) + 18\left(\tfrac{3}{20}\right) = \dfrac{91}{10} \).

questions.q: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures \(150^\circ\). How many sides does this polygon have?
questions.answer: Using the exterior angle method (much faster on the ACT than interior angles): Each exterior angle is supplementary to the interior angle: \(180^\circ - 150^\circ = 30^\circ\). Since the exterior angles of any regular polygon sum to \(360^\circ\): \(n = \frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ} = \mathbf{12} \mathrm{\ sides\ (dodecagon)}\)
questions.explanation: Using the exterior angle method (much faster on the ACT than interior angles): Each exterior angle is supplementary to the interior angle: \(180^\circ - 150^\circ = 30^\circ\). Since the exterior angles of any regular polygon sum to \(360^\circ\): \(n = \frac{360^\circ}{30^\circ} = \mathbf{12} \mathrm{\ sides\ (dodecagon)}\)

questions.q: An infinite geometric sequence has first term \(a_1 = 18\) and common ratio \(r = -\frac{1}{3}\). What is the sum of this infinite series?
questions.answer: Since \(|r| = |-\frac{1}{3}| < 1\), the infinite series converges. Using the formula \(S_\infty = \frac{a_1}{1 - r}\): \(S_\infty = \frac{18}{1 - (-1/3)} = \frac{18}{1 + 1/3} = \frac{18}{4/3} = 18 \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{54}{4} = \mathbf{\frac{27}{2}} \mathrm{\ (or\ } 13.5\mathrm{)}\)
questions.explanation: Since \(|r| = |-\frac{1}{3}| < 1\), the infinite series converges. Using the formula \(S_\infty = \frac{a_1}{1 - r}\): \(S_\infty = \frac{18}{1 - (-1/3)} = \frac{18}{1 + 1/3} = \frac{18}{4/3} = 18 \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{54}{4} = \mathbf{\frac{27}{2}} \mathrm{\ (or\ } 13.5\mathrm{)}\)

If \(\cos\theta = -\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant II, what is the value of \(\tan\theta\)?
questions.answer: In Quadrant II, \(x = -4\) and hypotenuse \(r = 5\). Using \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\): \((-4)^2 + y^2 = 5^2 \Rightarrow 16 + y^2 = 25 \Rightarrow y = 3 \quad (\mathrm{positive\ in\ QII})\) Therefore: \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{3}{-4} = \mathbf{-\frac{3}{4}}\).
questions.explanation: In Quadrant II, \(x = -4\) and hypotenuse \(r = 5\). Using \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\): \((-4)^2 + y^2 = 5^2 \Rightarrow 16 + y^2 = 25 \Rightarrow y = 3 \quad (\mathrm{positive\ in\ QII})\) Therefore: \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{3}{-4} = \mathbf{-\frac{3}{4}}\).

questions.q: If \(A = \left(2, -1 ; 3, 4\right)\) and \(B = \left(5 ; -2\right)\), what is the matrix product \(AB\)?
questions.answer: The product of a $2 \times 2\( matrix and a \)2 \times 1\( matrix is a \)2 \times 1\( column vector. Compute row by column: First row: \)2(5) + (-1)(-2) = 10 + 2 = 12\(. Second row: \)3(5) + 4(-2) = 15 - 8 = 7\(. Thus \)AB = \mathbf{\left(12 ; 7\right)}$.
questions.explanation: The product of a $2 \times 2\( matrix and a \)2 \times 1\( matrix is a \)2 \times 1\( column vector. Compute row by column: First row: \)2(5) + (-1)(-2) = 10 + 2 = 12\(. Second row: \)3(5) + 4(-2) = 15 - 8 = 7\(. Thus \)AB = \mathbf{\left(12 ; 7\right)}$.

questions.q: Line \(K\) passes through the points \((-3, 5)\) and \((1, -3)\). What is the slope of a line perpendicular to line \(K\)?
questions.answer: First calculate the slope of line \(K\): \(m_K = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{-3 - 5}{1 - (-3)} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\) A line perpendicular to \(K\) has slope \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{m_K}\): \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{-2} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{2}}\)
questions.explanation: First calculate the slope of line \(K\): \(m_K = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{-3 - 5}{1 - (-3)} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\) A line perpendicular to \(K\) has slope \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{m_K}\): \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{-2} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{2}}\)

questions.q: A right circular cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 8 cm. What is its total surface area in terms of \(\pi\)?
questions.answer: The total surface area includes the two circular bases and the lateral curved surface: \(\mathrm{TSA} = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h = 2\pi(3^2) + 2\pi(3)(8) = 18\pi + 48\pi = \mathbf{66\pi} \mathrm{\ cm}^2\)
questions.explanation: The total surface area includes the two circular bases and the lateral curved surface: \(\mathrm{TSA} = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h = 2\pi(3^2) + 2\pi(3)(8) = 18\pi + 48\pi = \mathbf{66\pi} \mathrm{\ cm}^2\)

questions.q: What is the equation of the circle with centre \((-2, 4)\) and radius \(5\)?
questions.answer: Using the standard equation \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\) with center \((h, k) = (-2, 4)\) and \(r = 5\): \((x - (-2))^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 5^2 \Rightarrow (x + 2)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 25\)
questions.explanation: Using the standard equation \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\) with center \((h, k) = (-2, 4)\) and \(r = 5\): \((x - (-2))^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 5^2 \Rightarrow (x + 2)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 25\)

questions.q: In a set of 7 integers: \(\{4, 7, 9, x, 14, 18, 20\}\) arranged in ascending order, the median is equal to the mean. What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.answer: Median of 7 sorted values is the 4th value: \(x\). Mean \(= \frac{4 + 7 + 9 + x + 14 + 18 + 20}{7} = \frac{72 + x}{7}\). Equating: \(7x = 72 + x \Rightarrow 6x = 72 \Rightarrow x = 12\).
questions.explanation: Median of 7 sorted values is the 4th value: \(x\). Mean \(= \frac{4 + 7 + 9 + x + 14 + 18 + 20}{7} = \frac{72 + x}{7}\). Equating: \(7x = 72 + x \Rightarrow 6x = 72 \Rightarrow x = 12\).

A data set consists of the numbers \(\{3, 7, 8, 12, 15, 18, 21\}\). What is the interquartile range (IQR) of this data set?
questions.answer: The median is \(12\). The lower half is \(\{3, 7, 8\}\) with \(Q_1 = 7\). The upper half is \(\{15, 18, 21\}\) with \(Q_3 = 18\). Thus \(\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 18 - 7 = 11\).
questions.explanation: The median is \(12\). The lower half is \(\{3, 7, 8\}\) with \(Q_1 = 7\). The upper half is \(\{15, 18, 21\}\) with \(Q_3 = 18\). Thus \(\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 18 - 7 = 11\).

questions.q: If every value in a data set is multiplied by \(3\) and then increased by \(5\), how is the standard deviation \(\sigma\) affected?
choices: It is multiplied by \(3\) and increased by \(5\)
questions.answer: Multiplying by a constant \(c\) scales standard deviation by \(|c| = 3\). Adding a constant shifts the center but does not change the spread. Hence, standard deviation is multiplied by \(3\).

questions.q: Which of the following data sets has a standard deviation equal to \(0\)?
questions.answer: A standard deviation of \(0\) occurs if and only if all values in the data set are identical.

questions.q: A bag contains \(6\) red marbles, \(8\) blue marbles, and \(10\) green marbles. If one marble is selected at random, what is the probability that it is NOT blue?
questions.answer: Total marbles \(= 6 + 8 + 10 = 24\). Non-blue marbles \(= 6 + 10 = 16\). Probability \(= \frac{16}{24} = \frac{2}{3}\).

questions.q: Two independent events \(A\) and \(B\) have \( P(A) = \dfrac{2}{3} \) and \( P(B) = \dfrac{3}{5} \). Find \( P(A \text{ and } B) \).
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. Independent events multiply: \( P(A)\times P(B) = \dfrac{2}{3}\times\dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5} \).

questions.q: In how many distinct ways can a committee of \(4\) members be chosen from a group of \(9\) people?
questions.answer: Selection order does not matter: \(\binom{9}{4} = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 126\).

questions.q: If the probability of an event is \( \dfrac{2}{15} \), what is the probability the event does NOT occur?
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. \( P(\text{not }A) = 1-P(A) = 1-\dfrac{2}{15} = \dfrac{13}{15} \).
